data.name: Poresh
data.gender_notes: Poresh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is the protector and ruler of the forest, often associated with the god Lord Shiva. The name Poresh carries the meaning “Lord of the Forest” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Poresh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the forest and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Poresh is a name that resonates with the spiritual essence of nature and the power of protection and rule. It is a name that is deeply connected to the Hindu deity Lord Shiva, who is the lord of the forest and the destroyer of evil.
data.etymology: Poresh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Forest.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Poresh total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Poresh was a chief of the Sesodia Rajputs, who ruled over the region of Marwar in present-day Rajasthan, India. He is believed to have lived during the late 12th or early 13th century.
historical_references.context: Ruler of the Sesodia Rajputs in Marwar

historical_references.reference: Poresh was a trusted general of Prithviraj Chauhan III, the last Hindu ruler of Delhi, during his wars against the invading Mongols led by Genghis Khan in 1221 AD. He lost his life while defending the fort of Takht-i-Sultan against Genghis Khan's forces.
historical_references.context: Trusted general of Prithviraj Chauhan III during wars against Mongols
